frame.question: How do we keep shipping pumps if our foundry stops again?
frame.whyNow: A fire closed our only foundry for eleven weeks last autumn, and 340 orders went out late.
frame.outcomeWanted: A stop at any one supplier costs us days, and the insurance for that is something we can afford every year.
boundaries: No more than $400,000 in the first year
No change to the approved pump designs

undo.how: Tooling at a second foundry cannot be moved. Stock can be run down over a year.

parts.name: Our foundry
parts.wants: Steady volume, and no rival on its best parts

links.note: Six in ten castings are poured in ten weeks
Every new source is inspected part by part

takes.why: Stock is the only thing we can undo.
Two parts cause most of the delay, so the cost of a second source can be kept to those.
The late-order list moved me: two parts, 81% of it.
It costs less than half of two full sources.

criteria.text: Keeps shipping through a ten-week stop
criteria.high: No order more than two weeks late

criteria.text: In place before the spring peak of 2026
Keeps our foundry on our side
criteria.low: It drops us down its list
criteria.high: It plans the spring with us

options.name: Second foundry for every part
options.because: Above the first-year limit, and 31 parts could not be inspected in time.

options.name: Twelve weeks of stock
options.because: Covers a stop once, then takes a year to rebuild.

options.name: Second source for two parts, plus stock
mustBeTrue: The two parts keep causing most of the delay

options.name: Pour our own
options.because: No room on site for a furnace.

evidence.text: Two of 31 cast parts were behind 81% of the late orders.
Two foundries quoted tooling for both parts at $118,000 and $131,000.
Second source and five weeks of stock come to about $200,000 in a year.
evidence.source: From the quotes and the stock list

evidence.text: Our foundry will not mind losing a fifth of two parts.
evidence.ifWrong: It puts other customers first in the spring.

evidence.text: How often a foundry of this size stops for a month or more.

outsideView.similarCases: Six firms in the trade group that added a second source since 2019
outsideView.whatHappened: Four were late getting the second source approved, by three to seven months

ratings.because: Either foundry can carry every part.
The two worst parts have a second door.

tensions.evidence: A second source for every part is above the limit.
tensions.result: Second source only for the two parts that cause most of the delay.
tensions.gaveUp: Cover for the other 29 parts beyond five weeks.

tensions.evidence: The foundry asked us to take some spring volume elsewhere.

objections.text: The second foundry will take longer to approve than you think.
objections.cheapestTest: Send one impeller for inspection before ordering the tooling.

objections.text: Stock hides the problem until it runs out.
objections.settledBy: Last autumn’s eleven weeks would have used all twelve.

objections.text: Our foundry will drop us down its list.
objections.settledBy: Its letter of 3 February asks us to move some spring volume.

failureStories.story: It is spring 2026. The second foundry is still not approved and the stock went to a big order in January.
failureStories.guard: Stock for the two parts is released only by Dana.

decision.reason: It opens a second door for the two parts that hurt us, at a price we can pay every year.
decision.givingUp: Cover for the other 29 parts beyond five weeks.
decision.firstStep: Send one impeller to each foundry for inspection this month.
decision.keepReversible: Order tooling for one part first.

steps.gate: One passes, or we talk again

steps.step: Five weeks of stock for all 31 parts

measures.measure: Orders more than two weeks late for castings

forecasts.claim: No order ships more than two weeks late because of castings
forecasts.howWeWillKnow: Shipping log, late orders by cause.

forecasts.claim: The second foundry passes first inspection on both parts by June
forecasts.note: The housing passed in May. The impeller passed in September.

forecasts.claim: The extra yearly cost stays under $210,000
Our first foundry keeps its prices within 5%

reopenIf.sign: No inspection date by the end of May
A third part passes 15% of late orders

review.whatHappened: No late orders for castings. The housing was approved in May and the impeller in September, three months after we expected. The first foundry stopped for nine days in November and nobody outside noticed.
review.process: Yes. Wen’s objection was the right one and the trial it asked for was run. We heard that four of six firms were late and still forecast June.
review.luck: The stop came after the impeller was approved. Three months earlier it would have tested the stock.
review.lesson: When the outside view gives a delay, start the forecast from it.

events.what: Widened the question from which foundry to how we keep shipping.
Both first takes written before either was shown.
Added two options: split, and pour our own.
Rated one criterion at a time; three options set aside.
Gave its own view from a fresh start, without the takes or ratings.
Stock set aside after the eleven-week check.
Chose split; four forecasts and two reopening signs recorded.
Said what happened first, then marked four forecasts.
